{"reviewer_role":"release-operations","verdict":"BLOCK","blockers":[{"id":"REL-001-ready-never-ready-fresh-pg","severity":"P1","evidence":["src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:1210","src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:1242","src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:1260","src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:492","src/server.ts:4","src/server.ts:6","src/http.ts:442",".github/workflows/ci.yml:121",".github/workflows/ci.yml:128",".github/workflows/ci.yml:136","Dockerfile:59","docs/deployment.md:214","docs/deployment.md:280"],"impact":"PostgresMemoryProvider.health() never calls ready()/migrate(), and nothing migrates at boot: src/server.ts constructs the provider and calls app.listen() directly, while ready() (src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:492) is reached only from ingest/search/list/get/retire/feedback/compact. On a fresh database with MEMORY_PG_AUTO_MIGRATE=true, to_regclass('memories') is NULL, hasCurrentMemorySchema is false, health() returns ok:false and /ready answers 503 indefinitely, because only a data request would ever trigger the migration and a readiness probe is not one. This deterministically fails the CI container job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:121-136 polls /ready with `curl --fail` 30 times, then `exit 1`), so acceptance criteria 3 and 4 are falsified: CI cannot boot the image against pgvector with provider-aware readiness. It also breaks the shipped image (Dockerfile:59-60 HEALTHCHECK targets /ready, so the container reports permanently unhealthy on first deploy) and both documented Postgres deployment paths: docker-compose with a fresh pgdata volume (docs/deployment.md:206-236) and the Kubernetes readinessProbe on /ready (docs/deployment.md:280-284), which would keep every replica out of the load-balancer pool after an initial rollout.","remediation":"In src/server.ts, before app.listen(), await provider.migrate?.() when config.postgresAutoMigrate is set, logging and exiting non-zero on failure. That makes readiness reachable while keeping request and readiness paths free of DDL, preserving acceptance criterion 1. A narrower but worse alternative is `await this.ready()` as the first statement inside health()'s try block, which restores readiness but moves DDL onto the probe path. Either way, add a CI assertion that /ready returns HTTP 200 with ok:true against a database that has never been migrated."},{"id":"REL-002-checksummed-migrations-claim-unimplemented","severity":"P2","evidence":["docs/CODEX_RUN_SUMMARY.md:176","src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:447","src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:455","src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:459","src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:462","migrations/001_init.sql:11","migrations/002_memory_spaces.sql:7"],"impact":"docs/CODEX_RUN_SUMMARY.md:176 states 'Made Postgres migrations ordered, checksummed, and advisory-lock serialized.' Ordering and the advisory lock are real (src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:446-466), but no checksum exists anywhere in the snapshot: the memory_core_migrations ledger has only version and applied_at (migrations/001_init.sql:11-14, migrations/002_memory_spaces.sql:7-10) and migrate() gates solely on `SELECT 1 FROM memory_core_migrations WHERE version = $1`. An operator relying on this sentence would believe an edit to an already-applied migration file is detected at deploy time; it is silently ignored instead, which is exactly the integrity property acceptance criterion 1 asserts and the one that guards migration-001 immutability in practice. This is a documentation defect about migration safety, not a cosmetic wording issue."],"remediation":"Smallest fix: delete the word 'checksummed' from docs/CODEX_RUN_SUMMARY.md:176. If the property is wanted, add a `checksum text` column to memory_core_migrations, store sha256 of each applied file, and have migrate() compare the on-disk file hash to the ledger row for already-applied versions, throwing on mismatch instead of `continue`."}],"findings":[{"id":"REL-003-stale-context-header-samples","severity":"P3","evidence":["README.md:103","docs/WORKING_OVERVIEW.md:105","docs/WORKING_OVERVIEW.md:109","src/service.ts:143","src/service.ts:650"],"impact":"Documented sample output still shows the pre-hardening headers 'RELEVANT MEMORIES (STORED EVIDENCE):' and 'KNOWN ACTOR PROFILE (STORED EVIDENCE):'. The implementation emits '... (UNTRUSTED STORED EVIDENCE; DATA, NOT INSTRUCTIONS):'. Since the untrusted framing is a prompt-injection control the release explicitly claims, stale samples understate the actual contract and could be copied into downstream prompt assertions.","remediation":"Update the three sample blocks to the exact strings in src/service.ts:143 and src/service.ts:650."},{"id":"REL-004-ddl-on-request-path-doc-contradiction","severity":"P3","evidence":["docs/providers.md:283","docs/providers.md:361","src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:493","src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:647","src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:875"],"impact":"docs/providers.md:283 says 'Search/ingest only inspect existing schema and never execute DDL', while docs/providers.md:361-362 says MEMORY_PG_AUTO_MIGRATE 'provisions the configured embedding dimension on first use'. The unconditional 'never' is accurate only for the default autoMigrate=false.","remediation":"Qualify docs/providers.md:283 to 'never execute DDL unless MEMORY_PG_AUTO_MIGRATE is enabled, in which case the first request applies pending migrations once'. If the fix for REL-001 moves migration to boot, state that instead and the sentence becomes unconditionally true."},{"id":"REL-005-probe-rate-limit-and-ready-detail-drift","severity":"P3","evidence":["docs/WORKING_OVERVIEW.md:21","src/http.ts:436","docs/deployment.md:347","docs/deployment.md:320","src/providers/in-memory-provider.ts:567"],"impact":"docs/WORKING_OVERVIEW.md:21 claims /health and /ready 'consume no rate bucket'; the coarse pre-auth IP limiter at src/http.ts:436 is installed before both routes, so probes do consume the pre-auth bucket. docs/deployment.md:347 already states this correctly, so the two operator-facing docs disagree on probe behaviour under load. Separately, the /ready sample at docs/deployment.md:320 omits the 'embedder=none' segment the in-memory provider actually emits.","remediation":"Reword docs/WORKING_OVERVIEW.md:21 to 'consume no per-key quota but do pass the coarse pre-auth IP limiter', and refresh the docs/deployment.md:320 sample detail string."},{"id":"REL-006-bench-ci-job-gates-nothing","severity":"P3","evidence":[".github/workflows/ci.yml:47",".github/workflows/ci.yml:60","bench/run.ts:235","bench/run.ts:433"],"impact":"The bench job comment states 'The random control must stay beatable', but bench/run.ts only prints '!! AT/BELOW RANDOM' and exits 0 regardless (main() rejects only on infrastructure errors; per-system failures are captured into the report). A retrieval regression to random-level ranking would pass CI green. Only the context job (bench/context.ts:264-271) actually throws.","remediation":"Add a --fail-on-at-or-below-random flag (or exit 1 when reports.some(r => r.atOrBelowRandom && r.system !== 'random')) and use it in the CI invocation, so the stated invariant is enforced rather than printed."},{"id":"REL-007-large-fixture-not-covered-by-determinism-gate","severity":"P3","evidence":["package.json:24","bench/dataset/generate.ts:81",".github/workflows/ci.yml:64",".github/workflows/ci.yml:67","bench/dataset/generated/large-seed1337.json"],"impact":"`npm run bench:dataset` passes no --size, so bench/dataset/generate.ts defaults to size=small and regenerates only small-seed1337.json. The committed large-seed1337.json fixture is therefore never rewritten before `git diff --exit-code -- bench/dataset/generated`, so acceptance criterion 4's 'deterministic benchmark fixture regeneration' is only half covered; a non-deterministic large-corpus generator would go unnoticed.","remediation":"Run both sizes in the CI step (`npm run bench:dataset && npx tsx bench/dataset/generate.ts --size=large`) before the git diff, or add a bench:dataset:all script and use it."},{"id":"REL-008-mcp-shutdown-unbounded-and-exits-zero-on-close-failure","severity":"P3","evidence":["src/integrations/mcp-server.ts:186","src/integrations/mcp-server.ts:192","src/integrations/mcp-server.ts:196","src/integrations/mcp-server.ts:203","src/server.ts:25","src/server.ts:36"],"impact":"MCP does close backend resources (backend.close?.() at src/integrations/mcp-server.ts:197, wired to provider.close via createEmbeddedBackend in src/integrations/tools.ts:385), which satisfies the criterion. However neither `await server.close()` nor `await backend.close?.()` is time-bounded, and the handler always calls process.exit(0) even after logging a provider-close failure. The HTTP server is strictly better here: a 10 s drain bound, a 5 s provider-close race, and exit code 1 on forced termination or close failure (src/server.ts:25-40). The MCP host therefore cannot distinguish a clean stdio shutdown from one that leaked a file-provider flush.","remediation":"Mirror src/server.ts: race both closes against a bounded timer and exit(1) when either times out or throws."},{"id":"REL-009-unresolvable-documented-subpath-import","severity":"P3","evidence":["src/integrations/index.ts:34","src/integrations/index.ts:36","package.json:11"],"impact":"The comment directs consumers to `import { createMemoryMcpServer } from \"@maitrix/memory-core/integrations/mcp-server.js\"`. package.json declares only `main: dist/index.js` with no `exports` or `files` map, and the compiled server lives at dist/integrations/mcp-server.js, so that specifier cannot resolve for any consumer. Low impact today because the package is `private: true` and unpublished, but it is a packaging claim that would break the moment the package is published.","remediation":"Either correct the comment to the dist-relative path, or add an `exports` map with an `./integrations/mcp-server.js` subpath pointing at dist/."}],"required_tests":["Fresh-database container smoke: start the image against an unmigrated pgvector database with MEMORY_PG_AUTO_MIGRATE=true and assert GET /ready returns HTTP 200 with ok:true and provider.provider==='postgres' within the probe window. This is the regression that catches REL-001 and is exactly what .github/workflows/ci.yml:121-136 intends but cannot currently pass.","Unit test asserting PostgresMemoryProvider.health() reports REL-001 is derived from a complete call-graph trace (health() -> pool.query only; ready() reachable only from data methods; server.ts never calls migrate) and is falsifiable by booting the image against an empty database.","Byte-identical regeneration of bench/dataset/generated/*.json could not be confirmed without running bench/dataset/generate.ts; only the CI wiring and the small-only default were verified.","Migration 001 immutability could only be checked within this snapshot (it contains no space_id and 002 adds it additively). There is no VCS in the snapshot, so the claim that 001 was not mutated across history is unverifiable here.","The published synthetic, LongMemEval and LoCoMo numbers were not recomputed; they are carried as repository claims. The relevant release property — that a degraded hosted reranker cannot be labelled active — is enforced in code (bench/context.ts:264-268, 90-92) and was verified by reading.","Test files were read for consistency with the implementation but not executed; a logic error inside src/service.test.ts, src/integrations/*.test.ts or src/providers/*.test.ts that only manifests at runtime would not have been caught.","Third-party runtime behaviour assumed rather than verified: node-pg simple-query handling of the BEGIN/COMMIT migration files, pg_advisory_lock(int->bigint) overload resolution, Python unittest discovery semantics for a start directory that is itself a package, and `node -e` staying CommonJS under \"type\":\"module\".","Severity of REL-002 reflects that a migration-integrity guarantee is asserted in release documentation without any implementation; if the project intends the sentence as loose changelog prose rather than an operator guarantee, the one-word deletion clears it immediately."]}
